# Results — Study 702 (Shark-Harmonic)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Scott
Carney's **Shark** ("5-0") harmonic: a five-point X-A-B-C-D structure where, unlike every other
member of the harmonic zoo, **neither leg is a retracement**. B extends the XA leg **1.13-1.618x
past point X**, C extends the AB leg a further **1.618-2.24x past point B**, and the completion
point D is a **ZONE at 0.886-1.13x the original XA leg** — the "5-0" band the brief asks us to
test. Believers read the B/C overshoot as exhaustion and expect price to resume the *original* XA
direction once D is touched. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Basket: SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, NVDA — identical to siblings
[699-butterfly-harmonic](../../699-butterfly-harmonic/), [700-bat-harmonic](../../700-bat-harmonic/)
and [701-crab-harmonic](../../701-crab-harmonic/), for apples-to-apples comparison.*

## The protocol

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Pivot detection | percentage-threshold zigzag on daily closes, **pct = 2%**; a pivot is recorded only at its **confirmation bar** (never the earlier, still-unconfirmed extreme) |
| Shark arm — structural bands (both arms) | AB **extends** XA past point X by **1.13-1.618x** (an overshoot, not a retracement — the Shark's first break from the rest of the zoo); BC **extends** AB past point A by a further **1.618-2.24x** |
| Shark arm — defining ratio | D is a **PRICE ZONE**, `[X + 0.886×(A−X), X + 1.13×(A−X)]` — the "5-0" completion band, a zone rather than the single-point targets used by Gartley/Bat/Butterfly/Crab |
| Placebo arm | identical structural pivots (same AB/BC bands, same candidate pool), but each candidate's D-zone is re-centered on a deterministic, seeded extension ratio drawn clear of [0.886, 1.13] (same zone half-width, 0.122) |
| D-zone scan | forward window of **120 sessions** from C's confirmation bar; first bar whose high-low range overlaps the zone |
| Execution | enter the fade at the touch bar's **own close** (the touch is observed intrabar via that bar's high-low range — one documented convention, identical in both arms) |
| Base-rate control | `n` random entry days per ticker, matched to the **same empirical bullish/bearish mix** as the real Shark touches, pooled over **20 seeds** — neutralizes the equity-drift confound a directional rule inherits on an upward-drifting tape |
| Bonferroni | pooled headline + 6 per-ticker splits (5-day) = **7 tests**; critical \|*t*\| raised from 2.0 to **2.69** (family-wise α = 0.05, normal approximation) |
| Costs | one round trip = **2 × one-way cost × NAV**; net figures at 5 / 10 bps one-way |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC) *t* of the mean return against 0 (events can cluster in time); Welch *t* for the base-rate and placebo arm-vs-arm comparisons; Wilson interval on hit rate |

No survivorship: six large, currently-listed single names/ETFs, individually named — not a
membership-conditioned panel.

## The headline — Shark XABCD, forward returns at D

Pooled confirmed pivots: **6,055** → Shark XABCD candidates: **103** → D-zone touches: **94**.

| horizon | n | hit rate | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 94 | 50.0% | +33.53 | +1.34 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **94** | **54.3%** | **+22.81** | **+0.42** |
| 10-day | 94 | 53.2% | +8.88  | +0.10 |

Hit rate (5-day): **54.3%** (Wilson 95% [44.2%, 64.0%]) — the interval straddles a coin flip. The
headline mean is small and positive, but nowhere near the *t* ≥ 2 bar at any horizon; if anything
the point estimate *fades* toward zero the longer the fade is held (10-day: +8.88 bps, *t* = 0.10).

## Per-instrument (5-day, gross)

| Ticker | *n* | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 11 | **+181.73** | **+4.63** |
| QQQ  | 12 | +112.75 | +1.24 |
| AAPL | 16 | +59.52  | +0.45 |
| MSFT | 14 | −46.53  | −0.48 |
| TSLA | 14 | +82.50  | +0.77 |
| NVDA | 27 | −98.65  | −0.72 |

Only SPY individually clears the uncorrected *t* ≥ 2 bar, on **n = 11** touches — too small a
sample for the HAC estimator to be trusted, and (see below) it does not survive the
Bonferroni-corrected comparison either. The other five tickers scatter around zero in both
directions; the pooled result is not driven by one dominant winner once SPY's small-*n* HAC *t*
is discounted.

## Signal axis — Shark fade vs a random-day BASE RATE, Bonferroni-corrected

The base rate redraws, per ticker and pooled over 20 seeds, the same number of random entry days
with the same empirical bullish/bearish mix as the real Shark touches — the equity-drift confound
a directional rule inherits on an upward-drifting tape.

| horizon | Shark mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps, n=1,880) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +33.53 | +1.73  | +1.14 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **+22.81** | −15.00 | **+0.60** |
| 10-day | +8.88  | −33.90 | +0.53 |

Per-ticker, 5-day, Shark vs its own matched-mix base rate:

| Ticker | Shark *n* | Shark mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 11 | +181.73 | −7.04  | +2.57 |
| QQQ  | 12 | +112.75 | −23.08 | +1.58 |
| AAPL | 16 | +59.52  | +31.08 | +0.24 |
| MSFT | 14 | −46.53  | −3.11  | −0.37 |
| TSLA | 14 | +82.50  | −0.45  | +0.36 |
| NVDA | 27 | −98.65  | −55.65 | −0.27 |

**Bonferroni correction across 7 tests** (pooled headline + 6 per-ticker splits, 5-day): critical
|*t*| = **2.69** (family-wise α = 0.05, normal approximation).

- **1 of 7 tests clears the uncorrected |*t*| ≥ 2 bar** (SPY, Welch *t* = +2.57, on just 11
  events).
- **0 of 7 survive Bonferroni.** The pooled point estimate (Welch *t* = +0.60) is nowhere near
  certified, and the one nominally-significant per-ticker split does not survive the honest price
  of having looked at the basket seven different ways.

## Tradability axis — the fade timer, net of costs

One round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV per event.

| hold | gross mean (bps) | net @ 5 bps (bps) | net @ 10 bps (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +33.53 (t=+1.34) | +23.53 (t=+0.94) | +13.53 (t=+0.54) |
| 3-day  | +31.95 (t=+0.87) | +21.95 (t=+0.60) | +11.95 (t=+0.33) |
| **5-day** | **+22.81 (t=+0.42)** | **+12.81 (t=+0.23)** | **+2.81 (t=+0.05)** |
| 10-day | +8.88 (t=+0.10)  | −1.12 (t=−0.01)  | −11.12 (t=−0.12) |
| 20-day | +32.38 (t=+0.21) | +22.38 (t=+0.14) | +12.38 (t=+0.08) |

No hold length ever clears *t* = 2 in either direction, gross or net, and the point estimate is
not even monotone in horizon (it dips negative net-of-costs at 10 days before drifting positive
again at 20) — the signature of noise, not a real, decaying edge. There is no horizon at which the
Shark's D-zone fade is both profitable *and* certified.

## Third axis (myth-check) — does the precise 0.886-1.13 zone beat a placebo completion zone?

Identical pivots and structural AB/BC bands; only the D-zone's *center* differs (Shark: fixed at
the 0.886-1.13 midpoint; placebo: re-drawn per-candidate, kept clear of that band by at least the
zone's own half-width).

| horizon | Shark mean (bps) | placebo mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +33.53 | +45.97 | −0.36 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **+22.81** | −0.68  | **+0.26** |
| 10-day | +8.88  | +56.13 | −0.42 |

Placebo candidates: 103 → placebo D-zone touches: 97.

Per-instrument, 5-day, Shark vs placebo:

| Ticker | Shark mean (bps) | placebo mean (bps) | beats placebo? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| SPY  | +181.73 | +125.53 | **yes** |
| QQQ  | +112.75 | +117.40 | no |
| AAPL | +59.52  | +191.56 | no |
| MSFT | −46.53  | −2.84   | no |
| TSLA | +82.50  | −29.97  | **yes** |
| NVDA | −98.65  | −183.40 | **yes** |

Shark beats the placebo on **3 of 6** tickers — a coin flip — and the pooled headline Welch *t* is
a negligible **+0.26**. Carney's specific 0.886-1.13 "5-0" completion band shows no detectable
edge over an arbitrary nearby zone built from the identical pivot geometry.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic mean-reverting price index (tunable `mean_rev` knob toward a slow EMA), pooled
across a **synthetic 6-name basket per seed** (mirrors the real pooled sample size); no network.

| world | *n* (pooled) | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`mean_rev = 0`), **20 seeds** | ~7/seed | — | mean **+0.08** (sd 1.07), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted `mean_rev = 0.70` (seed 702) | 132 | −92.35 | **−5.21** |

The null fires close to the nominal ~5% false-positive rate expected of a *t* ≥ 2 threshold over
20 independent draws (2/20 here), and a strong planted mean-reversion tendency lights up sharply
— the pipeline can find a real reversion effect when one is actually there. Note the sign:
because the synthetic world's reversion is a generic pull toward a slow moving average, not
specifically anchored to the Shark's own X-A geometry, the planted effect surfaces in the
*opposite* direction from the fade's `reversal_dir = sign(XA)` convention — this is expected and
does not weaken the check (it is a **power** proof, not a validation of the directional story).
This world needed a materially stronger knob (0.70) than the sibling Crab study's (0.12) to reach
the same significance, consistent with the Shark's D-zone (a band, not a point) diluting each
individual touch's signal. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Shark's 5-day fade-at-D return is **+22.81 bps/event, HAC *t* = +0.42**
  — small, positive, and nowhere near certified. Against the drift-matched base rate the pooled
  Welch *t* is +0.60, and **0 of 7 Bonferroni-corrected tests** (pooled + 6 per-ticker, critical
  |*t*| = 2.69) survive — the one nominally-significant split (SPY, Welch *t* = +2.57) rests on
  just 11 events and does not survive correction. Hit rate 54.3% (Wilson [44.2%, 64.0%]) straddles
  a coin flip.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No hold length (1/3/5/10/20 days) ever clears |*t*| = 2, gross or net;
  the point estimate is not even monotone in horizon, and by 10 days net-of-costs turns slightly
  negative before drifting positive again at 20 — the signature of noise. There is no horizon at
  which this trade is both profitable and certified.
- **"Beats a placebo completion zone (i.e. is 0.886-1.13 the Shark's defining edge, as Carney
  claims)?" — BUSTED.** The Shark arm beats its own placebo control on only 3 of 6 tickers (a coin
  flip), and the pooled 5-day Welch *t* (+0.26) shows no detectable specificity for 0.886-1.13
  over an arbitrary nearby zone built from the identical pivots — consistent with siblings
  [699-butterfly-harmonic](../699-butterfly-harmonic/), [700-bat-harmonic](../700-bat-harmonic/)
  and [701-crab-harmonic](../701-crab-harmonic/)'s finding that Fibonacci ratio labels add nothing
  over a randomized control on the same six tapes.
